title: When does a thing float?
question: If you change the weight, how does the part under water change?
steps: Drag the drum into the water.
Let go and watch the force pushing up.
Change the weight and compare how deep it sinks in.
observe: See how the buoyancy grows as more of the volume is under water.

terms.name: Buoyancy
terms.description: The force with which water or air pushes a thing up.

terms.name: Density
terms.description: How much mass is packed into the same volume.

terms.name: Volume under water
terms.description: The volume of the part of a thing that is in the water.

law.title: Buoyancy
law.description: The more volume is under water, the bigger the force pushing up.

tip: Drag the orange drum up or down with one finger into the water or above it and let go: it is let go right there (0.05 m steps). The blue arrow is buoyancy, the red arrow is weight. Change the drum's mass and volume and compare how deep it sinks in.
tip_short: Drag the drum up or down and let go

predict.question: If a small drum carries the heavy treasure chest, will it float?
predict.reason: The treasure chest is heavy, so the weight is bigger than the buoyancy. So the small drum sinks.

stages.text: Hang the empty chest on the small drum and float it!
stages.say: Water pushes a drum in it upwards. This force is called buoyancy. The empty chest is light, so buoyancy wins. So even the small drum floats.
stages.win: Bob, bob! The small drum floats!
stages.miss: Hang the empty chest on the small drum!

stages.text: What if the same small drum carries the treasure chest?
stages.say: The treasure chest is heavy. Its weight is bigger than the buoyancy, so the small drum sinks.
stages.miss: Hang the treasure chest on the small drum!

stages.text: Change to the big drum and bring up the treasure chest!
stages.say: A big drum pushes away a lot of water, so its buoyancy is big. So it floats up even with the heavy treasure chest.
stages.win: The treasure chest came up! I see the piece!

story.clue: The piece is in a treasure chest under the water! Let's float a drum and bring the chest up.
story.map_clue: Something sparkles under the pond's water!

kid.intro: This is the floating lab. Water pushes things in it upwards. This force is called buoyancy. The more water a drum pushes away, the bigger the buoyancy. Change the drum's size and the load! See whether it floats or sinks.
kid.title: Let's float a drum on the water!
kid.say: The deeper the drum is in the water, the harder the water pushes it up. A big drum pushes away a lot of water, so it floats even when heavy.
kid.tip: Drag the drum up or down and let go!

states.Not let go yet · drag the drum into the: Put the drum in the water

note.law: Water pushes the drum up as much as the volume under water. It floats when the buoyancy equals the weight.
